examples.ko: 설거지를 하고 나니 싱크대에 구정물이 가득해요.
examples.en: After doing the dishes, the sink is full of dirty water.
Please don't just dump the dirty water on the floor.

examples.ko: 구정물에 발이 빠져서 신발이 다 젖었어요.
examples.en: My foot sank into the dirty water and my shoes got soaked.
When I rinsed the rag, jet-black dirty water came out.

examples.ko: 그 개울은 구정물 냄새가 심해서 가까이 가기 싫어요.
examples.en: That stream smells so strongly of dirty water that I don't want to go near it.

examples.ko: 마당에 고인 구정물로 꽃에 물을 주면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't water the flowers with the dirty water pooled in the yard.

explain: 설거지나 걸레질 뒤처럼 집안일에서 나온 흐리고 더러운 물에 잘 써요. 그냥 '더러운 물'이라고 해도 되지만 구정물은 탁하고 지저분한 느낌이 더 강해요. 깨끗한 물은 '맑은 물'이라고 해서 짝으로 기억하면 좋아요.

phrases.en: Dirty water splashed because of a passing car.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더러운 물이 옷이나 몸에 튈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when dirty water splashes on clothes or skin.

phrases.en: I pour dirty water down the drain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쓰고 난 더러운 물을 치울 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when getting rid of used dirty water.

phrases.example: 비가 온 뒤에 길에 구정물이 고였어요.
phrases.en: After the rain, dirty water collected on the road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물이 한곳에 모여 있을 때 '고이다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: 고이다 is used when water gathers in one spot.

explain_en: It fits cloudy, dirty water left over from housework, like after washing dishes or rinsing a rag. You can also say '더러운 물', but 구정물 feels murkier and grimier. It helps to remember it as the opposite of '맑은 물' (clear water).

examples.en: When I drove a big nail into the wall, the cement cracked.
Be careful of the board with a big nail sticking out.
My father fixed the door firmly with big nails.

examples.ko: 낡은 다리에서 대못 몇 개가 빠져 있었어요.
examples.en: A few big nails were missing from the old bridge.
To pull out a big nail, you need a claw hammer.

examples.ko: 대못은 보통 못보다 훨씬 굵고 길어요.
examples.en: A big nail is much thicker and longer than a regular nail.

explain: 크고 굵은 못을 말해요. '대못을 박다'는 비유로 쓰여서 마음에 깊은 상처를 남기거나, 어떤 결정을 되돌리기 어렵게 만든다는 뜻이 돼요. 뉴스에서는 '규제에 대못을 박다'처럼도 나와요.

phrases.example: 그 한마디가 친구 마음에 대못을 박았어요.
phrases.en: drive a big nail into someone's heart
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음에 깊은 상처를 남길 때 써요. 또 어떤 일을 되돌리기 어렵게 확정해 버릴 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you leave a deep wound in someone's heart, or when you fix something so it is hard to reverse.
phrases.en_equiv: leave a deep scar; nail it down for good

explain_en: It means a large, thick nail. '대못을 박다' is also used figuratively, meaning to leave a deep wound or to make something hard to undo. In the news you also see it as '규제에 대못을 박다'.

examples.en: The hero in the film pulled the trigger.
That incident became the trigger of the war.

examples.ko: 손가락을 방아쇠에서 떼라고 훈련 교관이 말했어요.
examples.en: The training instructor told us to take our fingers off the trigger.
There's a safety catch near the trigger.

examples.ko: 작은 말다툼이 큰 싸움의 방아쇠가 됐어요.
examples.en: A small quarrel became the trigger of a big fight.

examples.ko: 장난감 총이라도 방아쇠에 손가락을 걸고 사람을 겨누면 안 돼요.
examples.en: Even with a toy gun, you shouldn't aim it at people with your finger on the trigger.

explain: 총 이야기에서는 '방아쇠를 당기다'라고 해요. 비유로는 어떤 일이 시작되는 계기를 '방아쇠가 되다'라고 말하는데, 뉴스나 글에서 더 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: become the trigger
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일이 시작되게 만든 계기를 비유로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Figuratively, the event that set something bigger off.

explain_en: For guns you say 방아쇠를 당기다. Figuratively, 방아쇠가 되다 means something sparked a bigger event, and this use is more common in news and writing.

t90.ax: The hero in the film pulled the trigger.

examples.ko: 백열전구는 값이 싸지만 전기를 많이 써요.
examples.en: Incandescent bulbs are cheap but use a lot of electricity.

examples.ko: 할아버지 댁 거실에는 백열전구가 달려 있어요.
examples.en: There is an incandescent bulb in my grandfather's living room.
The incandescent bulb kept flickering, so I bought a new one.

examples.ko: 백열전구를 찾으려고 마트를 두 군데나 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to two supermarkets looking for an incandescent bulb.
I learned that Edison invented the incandescent light bulb.
Don't touch the incandescent bulb, it's hot.

explain: 유리로 된 '전구' 그 자체를 말해요. 'LED 전구, 할로겐 전구'처럼 앞에 종류를 붙여서 구별하고, 말할 때는 '백열'을 빼고 '전구'라고만 해도 통해요.

phrases.en: The bulb burned out, so I have to buy a new one.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때는 '백열'을 빼고 이렇게만 해도 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: In speech you can drop 'baekyeol' and just say this.

phrases.en: I replaced the living room incandescent bulb with a new one.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래된 전구를 새것으로 바꿀 때 '갈다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '갈다' is used when swapping an old bulb for a new one.

phrases.example: 전기 요금 때문에 LED 전구로 바꿨어요.
phrases.en: I switched to LED bulbs because of the electricity bill.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 종류의 전구와 비교할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when comparing with other types of bulbs.

explain_en: The bulb itself, the replaceable part. It refers to the glass '전구' (bulb) itself. You attach a type in front, as in 'LED 전구' or '할로겐 전구', to tell them apart, and in speech you can drop '백열' and just say '전구'.

en: to suck in; to inhale; to soak in

examples.en: This vacuum cleaner sucks up dust powerfully.
The sponge soaked up water and became heavy.

examples.ko: 아이들은 새로운 말을 스펀지처럼 빨아들이는 것 같아요.
examples.en: Kids seem to soak up new words like sponges.

examples.ko: 숨을 크게 빨아들이고 천천히 내쉬어 보세요.
examples.en: Take a deep breath in and slowly breathe out.

examples.ko: 이 수건은 물을 잘 빨아들이지 못해요.
examples.en: This towel doesn't absorb water well.
That movie drew the audience in from the very start.

explain: 먼지, 물, 공기를 안쪽으로 끌어들일 때 써요. '관객을 빨아들이다'처럼 사람의 마음을 확 끌어당기는 비유로도 쓰고, 한자어로는 '흡수하다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 이 수건은 물을 아주 잘 빨아들여요.
phrases.en: This towel soaks up water very well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스펀지나 수건, 흙이 물기를 안으로 끌어들일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a sponge, towel, or soil draws moisture in.

phrases.en: This fabric absorbs sweat quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '빨아들이다'의 한자어로, 설명이나 글에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The Sino-Korean word for 빨아들이다, used more in explanations and writing.

phrases.example: 환풍기가 요리할 때 나는 연기를 빨아들여요.
phrases.en: The fan sucks in the smoke that comes from cooking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계가 연기나 먼지를 안쪽으로 끌어들일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a machine pulls smoke or dust inward.

explain_en: To absorb — pull in liquid or air, like towels or sponges (이 수건은 물을 잘 빨아들여요.) It is used when pulling dust, water or air inward. It also works figuratively, as in '관객을 빨아들이다' (to draw in an audience), and the Sino-Korean word is '흡수하다'.

examples.en: The market vendor carries goods with a handcart.

examples.ko: 할머니가 폐지를 실은 손수레를 밀고 가세요.
examples.en: An old woman is pushing a handcart loaded with scrap paper.
I loaded the handcart full of boxes.
The handcart's wheel came off, so I fixed it.
A handcart passed in front of the construction site.
Even though a handcart is small, it holds a lot of stuff.

explain: 사람이 손으로 밀거나 끄는 작은 수레예요. 일상에서는 '리어카'라고도 많이 말하고, 마트에서 쓰는 것은 '카트'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The man pulls a handcart to the market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 앞에서 당기는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a person pulling the cart from the front.

phrases.en: I loaded the luggage onto the handcart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 올려서 옮길 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when loading things to carry.

phrases.en: Grandfather came with vegetables loaded on a cart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 '손수레' 대신 많이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A word commonly used in daily life instead of 손수레.

explain_en: It is a small cart that a person pushes or pulls by hand. In daily speech it is also often called '리어카', and the kind you use in supermarkets is called '카트'.

examples.ko: 연필심을 너무 세게 누르면 자꾸 부러져요.
examples.en: If you press the pencil lead too hard, it keeps breaking.
Pencil lead is made from a material called graphite.

examples.ko: 연필심 끝이 뭉툭해서 글씨가 굵게 써져요.
examples.en: The tip of the lead is blunt, so my writing comes out thick.

examples.ko: 연필심이 다 닳으면 칼로 깎거나 새 연필을 쓰세요.
examples.en: When the lead wears down, sharpen it with a knife or use a new pencil.
Pencil lead dust got on my hand and made it black.
I wrote small letters with a sharp pencil lead.

explain: 연필 가운데의 까만 부분이에요. 샤프에 넣는 건 보통 '샤프심'이라고 불러서 구분해요. 그냥 '심'이라고만 해도 앞뒤 이야기로 알아들어요.

phrases.en: My pencil lead broke during the test.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연필심이 끊어졌을 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for when the lead snaps.

phrases.en: I wrote a lot, so the pencil lead is all worn down.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쓰다 보니 점점 짧아지거나 뭉툭해졌을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the lead gets worn or blunt from use.

phrases.en: I ran out of mechanical pencil lead.
phrases.nuance_ko: 샤프에 넣는 심은 '연필심'이 아니라 '샤프심'이라고 불러요.
phrases.nuance_en: Lead for a mechanical pencil is called 샤프심, not 연필심.

explain_en: It is the dark core in the middle of a pencil. The refill for a mechanical pencil is usually called '샤프심', which keeps the two apart. People may also just say '심' when the context is clear.

t90.ax: I wrote small letters with a sharp pencil lead.

en: to tie up; to fasten tightly

examples.en: It feels cool with my hair tied back.
I tied the boat to the post with a rope.

examples.ko: 짐이 떨어지지 않게 끈으로 단단히 잡아매세요.
examples.en: Tie the luggage tightly with a strap so it doesn't fall.

examples.ko: 자루 입구를 끈으로 잡아매고 나서 옮겼어요.
examples.en: I tied the mouth of the sack shut with string and then carried it.
I left the cow tied to a tree.
I tied my belt so tight that it's hard to breathe.

explain: 끈이나 줄로 단단히 묶어서 움직이지 않게 하는 것이에요. '묶다'보다 꽉 당겨 매는 느낌이 있어요. '머리를 잡아매다'처럼 머리카락을 묶을 때도 흔히 써요.

phrases.en: I tied my hair into one ponytail.
phrases.nuance_ko: '잡아매다'와 비슷하지만 더 일반적이에요. 꽉 당기는 느낌은 약해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 잡아매다 but more general, with less of a tight-pulling feel.

phrases.en: I tied the mouth of the sack tightly with a cord.
phrases.nuance_ko: 풀리지 않게 단단히 맨다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means tying firmly so it won't come undone.

phrases.en: I tied the cow to a tree.
phrases.nuance_ko: 움직이지 못하게 묶어서 그대로 둔다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means tying something so it can't move and leaving it that way.

explain_en: It means to bind something firmly with a string or rope so it does not move. It feels more like pulling tight than plain '묶다'. It is also commonly used for tying up hair, as in '머리를 잡아매다'.

t90.ax: I left the cow tied to a tree.

examples.en: I laid a thick carpet in the living room.
The carpet got dirty, so I sent it to the cleaner's.

examples.ko: 아이가 카펫 위에서 블록을 쌓고 있어요.
examples.en: The child is stacking blocks on the carpet.
Dust piles up easily because of the carpet.
The cat sharpens its claws on the carpet.

examples.ko: 이 카펫은 털이 길어서 청소기로 밀기 힘들어요.
examples.en: This rug has long fibers, so it's hard to vacuum.

explain: 방 전체에 까는 건 '카펫', 소파나 침대 앞에 까는 작은 건 '러그'라고 구분해서 말하기도 해요. 한국 집은 바닥이 따뜻한 온돌이라 카펫을 깔지 않는 집도 많아요. '카펫을 깔다', '카펫을 털다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: It's winter, so I laid a carpet in my room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바닥에 카펫을 펼쳐 놓을 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the most common phrase for laying a carpet on the floor.

phrases.en: I shook out the carpet on the balcony.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먼지를 없애려고 카펫을 흔들거나 두드릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it for shaking or beating a carpet to remove dust.

phrases.en: I put a rug in front of the sofa.
phrases.nuance_ko: 카펫보다 작은 깔개를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is for a smaller floor covering than a carpet.

explain_en: English loanword, everyday, common in homes and shops. People sometimes distinguish a '카펫' that covers a whole room from a small '러그' laid in front of a sofa or bed. Many Korean homes have heated ondol floors, so some homes don't use carpet at all. Common phrases are '카펫을 깔다' (lay a carpet) and '카펫을 털다' (shake out a carpet).

t90.ax: I laid a thick carpet in the living room.

examples.en: Add the oil once the frying pan has heated up.
The water heated up and began to steam.

examples.ko: 이 제품은 전자레인지에서 가열될 때 소리가 나요.
examples.en: This product makes a sound when it is heated in the microwave.

examples.ko: 오븐이 충분히 가열된 뒤에 빵을 넣어요.
examples.en: Put the bread in after the oven is fully heated.
The iron was heated and turned red.
The metal heats up too fast.

explain: 물이나 음식, 금속이 열을 받아 뜨거워질 때 써요. 열을 주는 쪽은 '가열하다'이고, 열이 지나치게 오른 상태는 '과열되다'라고 해요. 요리 설명서에는 '충분히 가열하세요' 같은 문장이 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: Wait until the oven is fully heated.
phrases.nuance_ko: 열이 충분히 올랐을 때 요리 설명에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common in cooking instructions when something has enough heat.

phrases.en: The meat wasn't heated enough.
phrases.nuance_ko: 열이 덜 올랐다는 뜻을 부정형으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says the heat didn't go high enough.

phrases.en: We grill meat on a heated stone.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가열된 + 명사'로 뜨거워진 물건을 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: '가열된 + noun' describes a thing that has been heated.

explain_en: Passive, something becomes heated, technical or descriptive. Use it when water, food or metal receives heat and becomes hot. The one applying heat uses 가열하다, and too much heat is 과열되다. Cooking instructions often say 충분히 가열하세요.

en: to be repeated; to occur repeatedly; to pile up

examples.en: Even when failures kept piling up, I didn't give up.
The same question kept coming up, and I got tired of answering.
As accidents kept happening, people became anxious.
My body is tired because of the repeated overtime.
If this keeps happening, you lose trust.
After repeated efforts, I passed the exam.

explain: '거듭되다'는 같은 일이 연달아 이어지거나 쌓일 때 써요. '반복되다'보다 글 같은 말이고, 실패, 사고, 노력, 논란처럼 계속 겹치는 일에 잘 어울려요. '거듭되는', '거듭된'처럼 뒤의 명사를 꾸밀 때 특히 많이 써요.

phrases.en: Despite repeated failures, I kept trying.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 겹친 일을 뒤의 명사에 붙여 말할 때 '거듭된'을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 거듭된 to attach an already-repeated event to the following noun.

phrases.en: I feel anxious because of the accidents that keep happening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금도 계속 이어지는 일에는 '거듭되는'을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 거듭되는 for something that is still continuing.

phrases.en: The same mistake keeps repeating.
phrases.nuance_ko: '거듭되다'보다 일상에서 더 자주 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler word used more often in daily life than 거듭되다.

explain_en: Written: problems or failures keep happening in succession, piling up. 거듭되다 is used when the same thing keeps happening one after another or piling up. It sounds more literary than 반복되다 and fits things that overlap again and again, such as failures, accidents, efforts, or controversies. It is especially common in the modifier forms 거듭되는 and 거듭된.

t90.ax: If this keeps happening, you lose trust.

en: to fall headlong; to fall head-first

examples.en: Because of the exchange rate, stock prices plunged.

examples.ko: 이번 학기에 제 성적이 곤두박질쳐서 걱정이에요.
examples.en: My grades plummeted this semester, and I'm worried.

examples.ko: 자전거가 언덕 아래로 곤두박질치는 걸 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw the bicycle tumble headlong down the hill.
They told me to be careful so my popularity doesn't plunge.

examples.ko: 내일은 기온이 갑자기 곤두박질칠 거라고 해요.
examples.en: They say the temperature will suddenly plunge tomorrow.

examples.ko: 사고가 난 뒤에 회사 이미지가 곤두박질치고 말았어요.
examples.en: After the accident, the company's image ended up plummeting.

explain: 성적, 주가, 인기, 기온처럼 수치나 평가가 한꺼번에 크게 떨어질 때 자주 써요. 반대로 빠르게 오를 때는 '치솟다'를 써요. '폭락하다'보다 말하기에 편한 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: Our team's results are plunging these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 현재 상황을 해요체로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite present form for describing a current situation.

phrases.en: I'm very worried about my plunging grades.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸며 주는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form that modifies a noun.

phrases.en: House prices crashed and it was on the news.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷하지만 값이 크게 내릴 때 쓰는 더 딱딱한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar, but a stiffer word used for prices dropping sharply.

explain_en: More common, vivid form; also figurative for sudden drops (주가가 곤두박질치다) It is often used when numbers or ratings such as grades, stock prices, popularity or temperature drop sharply all at once. When they rise rapidly, the word is '치솟다'. It feels easier in speech than the formal '폭락하다'.

t90.ax: I saw the bicycle tumble headlong down the hill.

examples.ko: 정부의 정책이 급선회를 해서 모두 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The government's policy made a sudden turn, and everyone was surprised.

examples.ko: 운전자가 급선회를 하는 바람에 차가 크게 흔들렸어요.
examples.en: The driver turned sharply, so the car shook a lot.

examples.ko: 회사의 급선회로 해외 진출이 갑자기 결정됐어요.
examples.en: The company's sudden change of course led to a sudden decision to expand overseas.

examples.ko: 비행기의 급선회는 승객에게 위험할 수 있어요.
examples.en: A sharp turn of a plane can be dangerous for passengers.
The team members were very flustered by this sudden turn.
Thanks to the sharp turn, I barely avoided an accident.

explain: 차, 배, 비행기가 갑자기 방향을 바꿀 때도 쓰고, 정책이나 계획의 방향이 갑자기 달라질 때도 써요. 뉴스에서는 '정책 급선회'처럼 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The bus suddenly made a sharp turn, which surprised me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '급선회'에 '하다'를 붙여 쓰는 가장 기본적인 짝이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic pairing, 급선회 with 하다.

phrases.en: Citizens were confused by the sudden policy reversal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스 제목에서 정책 방향이 갑자기 바뀔 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in news headlines when policy direction suddenly changes.

phrases.en: The ship rocked a lot because of the sharp turn.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 방향을 바꿔서 생긴 일의 이유를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to give the reason for something caused by a sudden turn.

explain_en: It is used when a car, ship or plane suddenly changes direction, and also when a policy or plan suddenly changes course. In the news it often appears like '정책 급선회'.

en: to fall forward; to topple over

examples.en: I tripped on a stone and pitched forward.
I fell flat while running and hurt my knee.

examples.ko: 그 회사가 갑자기 꼬꾸라질 줄 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I didn't know that company would suddenly collapse.
I dozed off and almost fell face-first onto the desk.
The bicycle tipped over forward and the load spilled out.
The tree was toppled by the wind.

explain: '넘어지다'보다 앞으로 거꾸러지듯 쓰러지는 느낌이 강해요. '고꾸라지다'와 같은 말이에요. 사람이 넘어질 때뿐 아니라 회사나 주가가 갑자기 무너질 때도 비유로 써요.

phrases.en: I almost tumbled forward on the stairs.
phrases.nuance_ko: '꼬꾸라지다'와 같은 말이라 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The same word as 꼬꾸라지다, so they are interchangeable.

phrases.en: The floor was slippery, so I almost fell on my face.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄹ 뻔하다'로 넘어지기 직전의 상황을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-ㄹ 뻔하다' describes a near-fall.

phrases.en: After the announcement, the stock price suddenly collapsed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비유로 가격이나 회사가 갑자기 무너질 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively when a price or company suddenly collapses.

explain_en: Colloquial; falling forward suddenly, tripping or collapsing. Compared with '넘어지다', it strongly suggests pitching forward headfirst. It means the same as '고꾸라지다'. Besides people falling, it is also used figuratively when a company or stock price suddenly collapses.

t90.ax: The tree was toppled by the wind.

examples.en: A pickpocket snatched my bag.
The eagle snatched the fish in an instant.
The child snatched the phone out of my hand.
He snatched the ball and ran straight toward the goal.
Someone snatched my umbrella and ran off.

examples.ko: 그 팀이 경기 막판에 역전 기회를 낚아챘어요.
examples.en: That team seized the chance for a comeback late in the game.

explain: 갑자기 힘 있게 잡아서 가져가는 순간적인 동작이에요. '빼앗다'는 억지로 가져가는 뜻이 강하고, 낚아채다는 재빠른 손동작이 눈에 보이는 느낌이에요.

phrases.example: 오토바이를 탄 사람이 제 휴대폰을 낚아채 갔어요.
phrases.en: A person on a motorcycle snatched my phone and left.
phrases.nuance_ko: '낚아채 가다'는 잡아서 그대로 가져갔다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '낚아채 가다' means to snatch something and take it away.

phrases.en: Please don't snatch the toy, because it scares the child.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정 명령형으로 갑자기 잡아당기지 말라고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative command telling someone not to grab suddenly.

phrases.en: The cat quickly snatched the ball.
phrases.nuance_ko: '재빨리'와 함께 쓰면 빠른 동작이 더 잘 드러나요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairing with 'quickly' highlights the swift motion.

explain_en: To grab quickly, like fishing, often from a hand or air. It is a sudden, forceful grab that takes something away in a moment. '빼앗다' stresses taking by force, while 낚아채다 gives a vivid picture of a quick hand movement.
